info.title: Hippo API
info.summary: Personal second brain — capture, nightly analysis, reading.
info.description:
Contract between the Hippo backend (Go, on the home NAS) and the Expo app and its share
extension. This file is the source of truth (ADR-0017): the Go server and the TypeScript
types are generated from it (ADR-0031), through `api/openapi.bundled.gen.json`, which
`make generate` assembles with the fiche components of `api/fiches.gen.json` (ADR-0035).

## Conventions

- Every route lives under `/api` and requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, except
  `/healthz` (ADR-0016). A missing or wrong token answers `401` before any routing.
- JSON in `snake_case`; dates in ISO 8601 UTC (`format: date-time`).
- Identifiers (ADR-0035): ULIDs for items, assets and batches; integers for categories and
  tags; content types are named by their `key`. An item references its category, content
  type and tags by identifier, never by name.
- Collections are paginated by cursor: query parameters `cursor` and `limit`; the response
  carries `next_cursor`, `null` on the last page.
- Nullability: a nullable value is declared on its property; in a `PATCH` body an absent
  field changes nothing and an explicit `null` clears the value.
- The fiche of an item is rendered by `fiche.template`, never by the item's content type:
  the two differ after a type correction (RG-60), a type merge (RG-72) or for a proposed
  type. `schema_version` tells which version of the fiche schema produced it (RG-64).
- Operations and schemas are binding. The status codes and problem types listed for each
  operation are provisional until the story that implements it, which amends them here
  first.
- An operation, request format or field declared here but not implemented yet answers
  `501` with the problem type `urn:hippo:problem:not-implemented`.
- The JSON body of an implemented operation is strict: a member this contract does not
  declare, or data after the JSON value, answers `400` with `about:blank` before the
  operation runs, so that a misspelt field is refused rather than silently ignored.
- A JSON body is 1 MiB at most; a larger one answers `413` with `about:blank`.

## Problem types

Errors use `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457, schema `Problem`); `detail` is in French
and can be shown as is. Generic HTTP errors (`400` for a request that breaks this
contract, `401`, `404` for an unknown route or another user's resource, `415`) use
`about:blank`. Business errors use one of these types:

| Type (`urn:hippo:problem:…`) | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid-url` | 400 | The URL of a capture is not a valid `http` or `https` URL (RG-02) |
| `empty-note` | 400 | The note of a capture is empty (RG-02) |
| `empty-capture` | 400 | The capture holds neither a URL, a note nor an image (RG-02) |
| `ambiguous-capture` | 400 | The capture holds a URL and a note, or a note and a capture note (RG-07) |
| `unsupported-image` | 400 | The image is not JPEG, PNG, HEIC or WebP (RG-02) |
| `image-too-large` | 413 | The image exceeds 20 MB (RG-02) |
| `private-item` | 409 | A private item is never sent to the AI (RG-12, RG-33) |
| `budget-exceeded` | 409 | The monthly AI budget is reached (RG-81) |
| `not-ready` | 409 | The item is still being extracted (RG-33) |
| `already-submitted` | 409 | The item is already in tonight's batch (RG-33) |
| `not-failed` | 409 | Only a failed item can be retried (RG-35) |
| `name-taken` | 409 | Another category under the same parent, or another tag, has this name (RG-54, RG-74) |
| `category-too-deep` | 400 | Categories have two levels at most (RG-51) |
| `category-not-empty` | 409 | Only an empty category can be deleted (backlog E4-07) |
| `invalid-merge-target` | 400 | A category, type or tag cannot be merged into itself or into its own subcategory (backlog E4-07) |
| `type-not-proposed` | 409 | Only a proposed content type can be merged into another one (RG-72) |
| `sync-expired` | 410 | The sync token is older than the 30-day retention of deletions: resync without a token (ADR-0035) |
| `not-implemented` | 501 | Declared in this contract, not implemented yet |

servers.description: Local backend on the Mac (make dev, make up)

tags.name: items
tags.description: Capture, read, correct and delete items

tags.name: review
tags.description: Morning review of what the AI classified

get.description: Liveness and readiness probe, used by the Docker healthcheck and the app settings screen. Public, no token required.

200.description: The service is up and its database is reachable.

503.description: The service runs but its database is not reachable.

post.description:
Creates an item from a link, a note (JSON body) or an image (multipart body) and answers
at once; extraction and analysis come later (RG-01 to RG-08). A duplicate link (same
normalised URL, RG-04, RG-05) or a replayed `client_id` (RG-08) returns the existing
item with `200`. A JSON body holds exactly one of `url` and `note`; a note capture holds
no `user_note` (RG-07). Surrounding whitespace is trimmed from `url` and `user_note`,
and a blank `user_note` counts as absent (RG-09). Until extraction runs, the title of a
link is the host name of its URL (RG-26). `source` defaults to `share`.

Checks, in order: `client_id` and `source` follow this contract (`400 about:blank`);
`url` with `note`, or `note` with `user_note` (`ambiguous-capture`); neither `url` nor
`note` (`empty-capture`); `url` not an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host
(`invalid-url`). A capture refused by a check stores nothing.

200.description: Existing item returned, in its current state. For a duplicate link (RG-04, RG-05), the capture note becomes the item's note if it has none, undated; otherwise it is appended after a blank line, prefixed by the day in Paris time (`2026-10-27 — note`), unless it equals a note already present. A duplicate marked `is_private` makes the item private; an unmarked one never makes it public (RG-15). The `url`, `source`, title and status of the item never change. A replayed `client_id`, including one merged into an existing item, changes nothing (RG-08).

400.description: Invalid capture: `invalid-url`, `empty-note`, `empty-capture`, `ambiguous-capture`, `unsupported-image`; `about:blank` for a body that breaks this contract (undeclared member, data after the value, malformed `client_id`, unknown `source`).

413.description: `image-too-large`, or `about:blank` for a JSON body over 1 MiB.

get.description:
Items of the user, newest first, pinned items first within a category (RG-77). `q`
searches the title, fiche, capture note, annotations and tags, ignoring case and
accents (RG-95); every filter combines with the others and with `q` (RG-96).
`category` includes its subcategories.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Tag id; repeat the parameter to require several tags.

parameters.name: unsorted
parameters.description: Only items without a category (À trier).

get.description: The item with its fiche and its images. An item of another user answers `404` (RG-90).

patch.description:
Changes the content type, category, tags, pin, annotations, capture note or private
flag. A change of content type, category or tags is recorded as a manual correction
(RG-60) that no reanalysis overwrites (RG-61). Unchecking private queues the item for
analysis again (RG-14).

delete.description: Deletes the item, its fiche, extracted content and images for good (RG-79); only a tombstone stays for the sync.

put.description: Records the reading position and moves the read status by RG-75, or forces read / unread.

post.description: Analyses the item at once, out of the nightly batch, at the full price (RG-33).
Puts a `failed` item back in the queue with its attempts reset (RG-35).

get.description: The image file of an item, as captured.
Items analysed since the last review, and the proposed categories and content types (RG-70).

post.description: Records the date of the review (RG-71); proposals left untouched come back next time (RG-73).

get.description: Every category of the user, active and proposed, flat with `parent_id` (two levels, RG-51).

400.description: `category-too-deep`, or a request that breaks the contract.

patch.summary: Rename, move, recolour a category, or accept a proposal
patch.description: Setting `status` to `active` accepts a proposed category; renaming a proposed category also accepts it (RG-72).

400.description: `category-too-deep`, or a request that breaks the contract.

post.description: Moves every item and subcategory of the category into the target, then deletes it (RG-72, RG-74); a merge that would create a third level is refused (RG-51).

400.description: `invalid-merge-target`, `category-too-deep`, or a request that breaks the contract.

get.description: Every content type, active and proposed, with the number of items of the user.

patch.summary: Rename or accept a proposed content type
patch.description: Accepts a proposed type by setting `status` to `active`; renaming a proposed type also accepts it (RG-72).

post.summary: Merge a proposed content type into another
post.description: Moves the items of the proposed type into the target and queues them for reanalysis, since their fiche is generic (RG-72).

400.description: `invalid-merge-target`, or a request that breaks the contract.

patch.description: The name is normalised (RG-58); a name already taken is refused, merging is the explicit gesture (RG-74).

400.description: `invalid-merge-target`, or a request that breaks the contract.

get.description:
Without `sync_token`, everything; with it, what changed since (ADR-0018, ADR-0035).
Rows come in change order, page by page; only the last page (`next_cursor` null)
carries the new `sync_token`, to send next time. Items never carry `content_text`.

parameters.name: sync_token
parameters.description: Token of the previous sync, as returned by its last page.

410.description: `sync-expired`: drop the cache and sync again without a token.

get.description: A zip archive with one Markdown file per item, in one folder per category, with front matter, fiche, annotations and images (RG-91). Generated on demand, never stored.
Items by processing status, queue size, failures and the cost of the current month (RG-82).

bearerAuth.description: Static API token shared by the backend (`API_TOKEN`) and the app, injected at build time (ADR-0016).

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor returned as `next_cursor` by the previous page. Omit it for the first page.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of entries in the page.

Problem.description: A problem document; its `type` tells which.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer token is missing or wrong.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or belongs to another user (RG-90).

type.description: Problem type. `urn:hippo:problem:<slug>` for business errors, `about:blank` otherwise.

title.description: Short summary of the problem type, in English.

detail.description: Explanation of this occurrence, in French, that the app can display as is.
examples: Le budget IA du mois est atteint : l'analyse reprendra le 1er du mois prochain.

instance.description: Path of the request that failed.

version.description: Version of the running backend (git revision, or `dev`).

ContentTypeKey.description: Key of a content type, in English snake_case (`tech_article`, `recipe`…).

CaptureSource.description: Where the capture comes from (`rss` arrives with V2).

ProcessingStatus.description: Where the item is in the pipeline (glossary "Statut de traitement").

ReadStatus.description: Where the user is in reading (glossary "Statut de lecture").

ExtractionMode.description: `full`: main content extracted; `fallback`: metadata only (RG-23); `none`: image or note.

ProposalStatus.description: `proposed` by the AI and not yet accepted, or `active` (RG-53, RG-57).

CorrectedField.description: A field the user corrected by hand (RG-60).

Asset.description: An image of an item, stored on the NAS.

ItemSummary.description: An item as shown in a list (cards of the library and of the review).

content_type.description: Content type key; null until analysed or sorted.

reading_minutes.description: Reading time of the original, computed at extraction (RG-25).

content_ok.description: False when the AI found the content too poor (RG-37); null until analysed.

Item.description: An item with everything shown on its fiche screen and kept in the offline cache. Never carries the extracted content.

title.description: Original title before analysis, then the title written by the AI.

user_note.description: Capture note; the content itself for a note item (RG-03).

content_truncated.description: The extracted content exceeded the limit and was cut (RG-24).

content_type.description: Content type key; null until analysed or sorted.

content_issue.description: What is missing, according to the AI (RG-37).

schema_version.description: Version of the fiche schema that produced the fiche (RG-64).

last_error.description: Why the last analysis failed, shown with the Relancer button (RG-35, RG-36).

CaptureRequest.description: A link or a note. Exactly one of `url` and `note`; a note holds no `user_note` (RG-07).

source.description: Where the capture comes from; `share` when absent.

client_id.description: Chosen by the device; a capture replayed with the same id returns the existing item (RG-08).

CaptureImageRequest.description: An image capture (screenshot or photo), 20 MB at most (RG-02).

source.description: Where the capture comes from; `share` when absent.

ItemPatch.description: Fields to change; absent fields stay as they are, `null` clears a nullable field.

category_id.description: New category; null moves the item to À trier.

tags.description: Replaces the tags of the item; names are normalised (RG-58), new ones are created.

ReadingProgress.description: The reading position, a forced read status, or both.

description.description: Helps the AI file the next items (RG-52).

parent_id.description: Root category when null (two levels at most, RG-51).

color.description: Accent colour set on this category; null inherits from the root (RG-59).

item_count.description: Items in the category and its subcategories.

parent_id.description: New parent; null makes it a root category.

name.description: Name shown in the app, in French.

has_template.description: False for a type rendered with the generic template (RG-57).

name.description: Lowercase, words separated by hyphens, no accent (RG-58).
Normalised by the backend like any tag (RG-58).

items.description: Items analysed since the last review (RG-70).

queue_size.description: Items waiting for the next batch.

month_cost_usd.description: AI cost of the current month, from the tokens really used (RG-80, RG-82).

budget_reached.description: No analysis until the 1st of next month (RG-81).

ItemTombstone.description: A deleted item; nothing but its id stays (RG-79).

KeyTombstone.description: A deleted (merged) content type; its id is its key.

SyncPage.description: One page of changes. The `item_count` of categories, content types and tags reflects the moment the row changed; the app recomputes the counts from its cache rather than relying on them after a delta sync.

next_cursor.description: Cursor of the next page of this sync; null on the last page.

sync_token.description: Token to send at the next sync; set on the last page only.

FicheText.description: Texte en français. Mise en forme autorisée : **gras** et `code` en ligne uniquement. Pas de titres, pas de listes, pas de liens Markdown.

caption.description: Courte légende facultative expliquant ce que fait ce code.

code.description: Code, commande ou configuration recopié À L'IDENTIQUE depuis la source. Ne jamais reformuler, tronquer ni traduire.

language.description: Langage pour la coloration : java, go, sql, bash, yaml, json, typescript, etc. « text » si inconnu.

code.description: Extraits de code liés à cette section, recopiés à l'identique.

sections.description: Le contenu détaillé, organisé en sections. Liste vide si le résumé suffit.

idea.description: L'idée reformulée proprement, fidèle à ce que Ghislain a écrit ou dicté. Corriger la forme (dictée, fautes), jamais le fond.

key_points.description: Points clés de la note. Liste vide si la note tient en une idée.

leads.description: Pistes à creuser ou questions ouvertes que la note mentionne. Liste vide si aucune : ne pas en inventer.

url.description: Uniquement une URL présente dans la source. Ne jamais en inventer.

address.description: Adresse complète si la source la donne. null sinon : ne jamais deviner une adresse.

best_time.description: Meilleur moment pour y aller, si la source le dit. null sinon.

maps_query.description: Texte à chercher dans Plans pour trouver le lieu : nom + adresse ou ville.

place_kind.description: Nature du lieu en un ou deux mots : restaurant, bar, café, musée, parc, balade, boutique, ville, hébergement…

practical_info.description: Infos pratiques données par la source : horaires, prix, réservation, accès. Liste vide si aucune.

website.description: Site officiel s'il figure dans la source.

what_to_do.description: Ce qu'on y fait, ce qui le rend intéressant, ce qu'il faut commander ou voir.

cook_minutes.description: Temps de cuisson en minutes. null si la source ne le donne pas : ne pas estimer.

ingredients.description: Tous les ingrédients, avec leurs quantités exactes.

group.description: Sous-partie de la recette si la source en a (« Pâte », « Garniture »).

quantity.description: Quantité et unité telles que données (« 200 g », « 1/2 c. à café », « une pincée »). null si non précisée.

prep_minutes.description: Temps de préparation en minutes. null si la source ne le donne pas : ne pas estimer.

servings.description: Nombre de portions tel que donné (« 4 personnes », « 12 cookies »). null si inconnu.

steps.description: Toutes les étapes, dans l'ordre, avec températures et durées.

tips.description: Conseils, variantes et conservation mentionnés par la source. Liste vide si aucun.

alternatives.description: Alternatives citées par la source. Liste vide si aucune : ne pas en ajouter de sa propre initiative.

pricing.description: Licence ou prix si la source le précise (« open source, MIT », « gratuit jusqu'à 3 projets »). null sinon.

url.description: Lien principal de la ressource s'il figure dans la source.

what_it_is.description: Ce que c'est, en une ou deux phrases (outil en ligne de commande, librairie Java, service SaaS, repo…).

when_to_use.description: Dans quel cas le choisir plutôt qu'autre chose, si la source permet de le dire. null sinon.

details.description: Les détails techniques, organisés en sections. AUCUNE information utile ne doit manquer : versions, chiffres, options, commandes, code, comparaisons, benchmarks.

key_changes.description: Ce qui change ou ce qu'il faut retenir, une idée par entrée. Liste vide si l'article ne décrit pas de changement.

links.description: Liens utiles présents dans la source (documentation, JEP, repo). Liste vide si aucun.

pitfalls.description: Limites, pièges, incompatibilités, avertissements mentionnés par la source. Liste vide si aucun.

tldr.description: L'essentiel en quelques lignes (2 à 5 phrases) : de quoi il s'agit et pourquoi ça compte.

versions.description: Produits et versions cités comme sujet de l'article (affichés en badges). Liste vide si aucun.

materials.description: Matériel ou produits nécessaires, avec les quantités si la source les donne. Liste vide si aucun.

steps.description: Les étapes courtes, dans l'ordre. Liste vide si l'astuce tient en une phrase.

warnings.description: Précautions mentionnées par la source (surfaces à éviter, mélanges dangereux…). Liste vide si aucune.

expected_result.description: Comment vérifier que ça a marché. null si la source ne le dit pas.

goal.description: Ce qu'on obtient à la fin, en une ou deux phrases.

prerequisites.description: Ce qu'il faut avoir ou savoir avant de commencer, avec les versions si la source les donne. Liste vide si aucun.

steps.description: Toutes les étapes, dans l'ordre. Ne jamais en fusionner au point de perdre une action.

troubleshooting.description: Erreurs courantes et solutions données par la source. Liste vide si aucune.

Fiche.description: Fiche of an item, in the format of its template (docs/prompt/schemas/fiches). Render it by its template, never by the content type of the item.
